title: kubectl, Pods and Deployments
description: Ten questions covering the CLI, the Pod lifecycle, probes, labels and how Deployments manage ReplicaSets. Includes fill-in-the-command questions graded with fuzzy matching.

questions.prompt: A Pod named 'api' is in CrashLoopBackOff. Write the command that shows the logs of the container instance that just crashed.
questions.explanation: The current container has only just started and has printed nothing useful. --previous (-p) shows the output of the instance that terminated, which is where the actual error is.

questions.prompt: A Pod is Running and its container is healthy, but the Service in front of it sends no traffic to it. Which probe should you inspect first?

options.text: livenessProbe
readinessProbe
startupProbe
None - probes do not affect Service routing

questions.explanation: A failing readiness probe removes the Pod from the Service's endpoints without restarting it, which is exactly this symptom. A failing liveness probe would restart the container instead.

questions.prompt: kubectl describe pod shows Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137. What happened?

options.text: The container exceeded its CPU limit and was throttled to a halt
The container exceeded its memory limit and the kernel killed it
The liveness probe failed three times in a row
The node ran out of disk and evicted the Pod

questions.explanation: Exit code 137 is 128 + 9 (SIGKILL), and OOMKilled names the cause. Exceeding a CPU limit only throttles the container - it is never killed for CPU.

questions.prompt: Write the command that outputs the YAML for a Deployment named 'web' using image nginx with 3 replicas, without creating anything in the cluster.
accepted_answers: kubectl create deployment web --image nginx --replicas 3 --dry-run=client -o yaml
questions.explanation: --dry-run=client -o yaml is the scaffolding pattern that saves the most time in the exam: generate, redirect to a file, edit the fields the generator cannot produce, then apply.

questions.prompt: A Deployment with 3 replicas has its image changed once. After the rollout completes, what do you see?

options.text: One ReplicaSet with 3 replicas; the old one is deleted
Two ReplicaSets: the new one with 3 replicas, the old one scaled to 0
Two ReplicaSets, each with 3 replicas
One ReplicaSet whose Pod template was updated in place

questions.explanation: Each template change creates a new ReplicaSet. The old one is retained at zero replicas (up to revisionHistoryLimit) which is exactly what makes kubectl rollout undo instant.

questions.prompt: You try to change spec.selector.matchLabels on an existing Deployment and the API server rejects it. Why?

options.text: The selector is immutable after creation
You lack RBAC permission to patch selectors
Selectors can only be changed while the Deployment is paused
The change is valid; the error means the labels are malformed

questions.explanation: spec.selector is immutable on Deployments, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets and DaemonSets. Changing it requires deleting and recreating the object.

questions.prompt: Which statements about labels and annotations are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Labels can be used in selectors; annotations cannot
Annotation values may be much larger than label values
A Service's spec.selector supports matchExpressions
kubectl label pod web env- removes the env label

questions.explanation: A Service selector is a plain map supporting only equality matching; matchExpressions is available to Deployments, ReplicaSets and NetworkPolicies. The trailing dash syntax removes a label or annotation.

questions.prompt: A ConfigMap consumed as environment variables has changed. Write the command that recreates the Pods of Deployment 'web' so they pick up the new values.
questions.explanation: Environment variables are injected at container start and never updated in place. rollout restart triggers a normal rolling replacement without changing the template.

questions.prompt: Which of these can leave a Pod in Pending? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Insufficient allocatable CPU or memory on every node
A nodeSelector label that no node carries
An unbound PersistentVolumeClaim
A taint that the Pod does not tolerate
A failing liveness probe

questions.explanation: Pending means the Pod has not been bound to a node, so every cause is a scheduling constraint. A liveness probe only runs once the container is already started, so it causes restarts, not Pending.

questions.prompt: A Deployment reports Progressing=False with reason ProgressDeadlineExceeded. What does Kubernetes do next?

options.text: It automatically rolls back to the previous revision
It stops making progress and waits for you to intervene
It deletes the failing ReplicaSet and retries from scratch
It scales the old ReplicaSet back to full capacity

questions.explanation: There is no automatic rollback. The condition is a signal for you or your CI system to run kubectl rollout undo. The old ReplicaSet keeps whatever replicas it had, which is why the app is usually still partly available.
